annotation.tension: Unlike the other personas, this one IS explicitly resolved — but only in the final session, with clear correction language ('correction... it's actually $95k now, not $120k'). Included as a contrast case: a real, explicit correction embedded in ordinary conversation rather than a dated memo.
annotation.why_unresolved: It isn't unresolved by the end, but for most of the conversation's history it looks exactly like the earlier personas' silent contradictions — the test is whether a provider correctly weights the explicit correction once it arrives, rather than treating all three numbers ($120k, the derived $48k/$36k/$36k split, and $95k) as equally valid.
annotation.good_response_looks_like: Using $95k as the current budget and correctly redoing the channel split proportionally (40/30/30 of $95k = $38k / $28.5k / $28.5k), while being able to mention the prior $120k figure as superseded if asked about history.
failure_modes_to_watch_for: Keeps using the stale $120k figure or the derived $48k/$36k/$36k split after the correction.
Applies the correction but recomputes the split incorrectly.
Treats the correction as if it were ambiguous/unresolved (hedging) when the user was actually explicit — over-hedging is its own failure mode, not just under-hedging.
